+# Measurements
+
+These are single-run proof-of-concept measurements, not benchmarks. Shared caches were retained. Failed attempts remain in the individual JSON records. Image `started_utc` fields written by the build helper were captured after the command; monotonic `seconds` is the duration used below. Do not use that helper field as an exact start time.
+
+## Environment
+
+macOS 27.0.1 build 26A434, Darwin 27.0.0, ARM64 Apple M5 Max, 18 logical CPUs, 137,438,953,472 bytes RAM (128 GiB). Initial free disk was 2,007,956,910,080 bytes (the adjacent initial probes vary slightly). Docker client 29.9.2; OrbStack Linux ARM64 engine 29.8.2. See `environment.json` and the recorded disk checks. The local disk-threshold policy was explicitly waived by the user; shared cache pruning was not used.
+
+## Image builds
+
+| Build | Duration | Cache condition and result | Evidence |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| First small image attempt | 16.509 s | Failed npm CLI copy layout; retained | `image/build-2.1.310-cold.json` |
+| Corrected first small image | 18.875 s | First successful derived recipe; host base layers partly cached | `image/build-2.1.310-retry.json` |
+| Construct-based v2 image | 25.886 s | New recipe; existing base/tool download caches | `image/poc-final-v2.json` |
+| Unchanged v2 recipe | 1.705 s | Build instructions reused cache; no shared cache eviction | `image/poc-final-build-matrix.json` |
+| Forced v2 rebuild | 30.908 s | `--no-cache`; base image layers remain cached | Same matrix |
+| Actual agent version change to 2.1.309 | 24.847 s | Same recipe/tooling, changed npm agent version | Same matrix + sandbox version record |
+| Final Rust-ready v3 | 75.029 s | Added compiler/linker dependencies and locked-project prefetch; warm host image cache | `image/poc-v3-buildessential-prefetch.json` |
+
+The warm/forced v2 build manifests have different recorded IDs; cache reuse is established by cached instruction output, not by asserting identical manifest IDs. The v3 recipe is a later distinct experiment. No fully empty host-image/build cache was created, and the v2 numbers are not v3 cold/warm results.
+
+## Readiness and first development test
+
+| Measurement | Observed duration | Definition and cache condition |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| First container sandbox create command | 0.765 s | CLI completion, local image present; **not** an independently polled readiness time |
+| First independent Ready observation | 7.044 s after create request | Basic get showed Ready; includes manual delay, so this is an observation bound rather than isolated provisioning latency |
+| Warm SDK sandbox start | 0.700 s | SDK response contained phase Ready; same image and retained workspace |
+| Primary sandbox warm start | 1.292 s | CLI start plus subsequent retained-file/Docker checks; image cached |
+| First successful native development test | 174.024 s after first create request | Rust compile/run passed; includes uploads, tool-home correction and unrelated interactive probes, not pure build time |
+| VM first Ready observation | about 72 s | VM profile runtime/image disks initially cold; source Docker image already cached |
+| VM create to successful offline compile | about 122 s | Includes env diagnosis and file upload; same local v3 image |
+
+| Dedicated daemon readiness | Duration | Criterion |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| cold | 0.413 s | First successful mTLS Docker info; host image cached; fresh empty daemon data |
+| warm | 1.474 s | First successful mTLS Docker info; host image cached; same daemon data retained |
+
+The daemon timing fixture used a fresh dedicated engine, distinct generated trust root, pinned Docker 29.8.2 DinD image, 1 CPU/512 MiB limit, and loopback-only published API port 18779. Cold means empty daemon data with host image layers already present. Warm means restart of the same fixture with its data retained; shutdown/restart overhead is included. Commands, failed readiness polls if any, authenticated response and exact fixture removal are in `measurements/daemon-authenticated-readiness.json`. Its cleanup was script-owned. Earlier startup-log listener timing (0.292 s) and an empty Engine B restart (1.572 s) are supplemental and are not substituted for authenticated cold readiness.
+
+The Docker-executed Rust workaround compiled and ran the native loopback test in about 51.08 s cold, with a warm execution around 0.365 s. It changed execution location and returned a file by explicit copy. These are not measurements of native external-network compatibility.
+
+## Resource use
+
+`resources-idle.json` sampled the early container profile: basic agent approximately 5.9 MiB, its separate supervisor approximately 18.8 MiB, and each idle dedicated engine approximately 64–65 MiB. These are snapshots, not guaranteed steady-state baselines.
+
+`measurements/rust-agent-peak.json` read cgroup `memory.peak`: 1,915,482,112 bytes, with 175,132,672 bytes current and a 4 GiB cap. `measurements/engine-a-peak.json` recorded a 4 GiB cgroup peak at the 4 GiB cap; that ancestor includes image loading, daemon, builders and child containers. The samples were taken during/after the experiments, so peaks are not attributed solely to one operation. No whole-machine peak or combined VM host/guest utilization was measured.
+
+The separate 64 MiB agent test killed a 128 MiB allocation (status 137); `memory.events` changed from zero kills to `oom_kill 1`. The supervisor is outside that agent cap. Dedicated engines had separate 2 CPU/4 GiB ancestor caps; a child reported 0.5 CPU/128 MiB. These are separate budgets. VM effective configuration was 2 vCPUs/2048 MiB, not the ignored `--cpu 1` request.
+
+## Cleanup
+
+VM instance deletion removed its overlay and exact instance processes, leaving about 6.2 GiB of experiment-owned prepared-image cache until the VM fixture script removed it. The VM profile directory dropped from about 6.3 GiB allocated runtime state to about 40 KiB of retained scripts/config/log evidence. The previous preview VM remained active.
+
+The independent disk helper removed 12 exited experiment orphan containers and 10 unused experiment image tags, after recording exact IDs and volume references. Top-level cleanup removed remaining experiment sandboxes, external engines and their children, approved project/socket volumes, identified channel volumes, experiment image tags, generated keys and local SDK venv. These removals were not shared-cache pruning. See `cleanup/execution.json`, `disk-audit/`, and final inventories.
+
+Top-level cleanup free-space observations: before 2,037,538,013,184 bytes; after 2,045,334,794,240 bytes. Concurrent writes prevent attributing this difference solely to cleanup.
+
+## Material limitation of the environment run
+
+Three pre-existing OpenShell Docker sandboxes were running in the first inventory and were later found stopped (exit 137 at 22:14:39 UTC). The first test gateway temporarily used their default Docker namespace; later controlled tests proved cross-gateway namespace interference and the unique-label configuration removed it. The initial termination actor is not proven because the first gateway startup log was not retained. These stops predate final cleanup. See `collateral/gateway-analysis.md`; restoration was separately authorized under the original experiment-only mutation limit. Guarded original-gateway stop/start and post-restoration exec checks passed for the same three IDs; see `collateral/restore-originals-execution.json` and `collateral/restoration-verification.json`. This collateral effect is not hidden by the successful isolated runs.
+
+The final disk-helper audit additionally found and removed 12 unreferenced `openshell-supervisor-*` volumes tied by exact sandbox UUID/namespace/managed-by/backend labels to the old experiment instances. They were missed by the first mounted-volume inventory. Their labels, no-reference checks and removal statuses are retained in `disk-audit/supervisor-volume-cleanup.json`; no contents were read. Final audit found no experiment tags, containers, volumes, listeners or generated private keys. Shared public image/build caches remain.

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Alexey Zhokhov
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+FROM projectjackin/construct:0.37-trixie@sha256:67fc093e1dd9a021e2af66beebbeddbb4d676839dcd0a5371ce8a5d7b2cdcab4
+
+SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-o", "pipefail", "-c"]
+
+ARG CARGO_BINSTALL_VERSION=1.23.0
+ARG OPENTOFU_VERSION=1.12.6
+# CAVEMAN_VERSION must be tagged release.
+ARG CAVEMAN_VERSION=2.7.0
+ARG CTX7_VERSION=0.5.11
+ARG SKILLS_VERSION=1.5.22
+# HEADROOM_VERSION.
+ARG HEADROOM_VERSION=0.37.0
+# UV_VERSION.
+ARG UV_VERSION=0.12.15
+# RTK_VERSION (aqua).
+ARG RTK_VERSION=0.49.0
+
+USER root
+RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt,sharing=locked \
+    --mount=type=cache,target=/var/lib/apt,sharing=locked \
+    apt-get update && \
+    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
+    build-essential \
+    libssl-dev \
+    openssl \
+    pkg-config \
+    cmake \
+    xxd && \
+    apt-get autoremove -y
+
+USER agent
+
+ENV MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS=/workspace:/tmp/jackin-mise
+
+COPY --chown=root:root jackin-toolchain/ /tmp/jackin-mise/
+
+RUN mkdir -p \
+    "${HOME}/.cache/amp" \
+    "${HOME}/.cache/mise" \
+    "${HOME}/.cargo/bin" \
+    "${HOME}/.cargo/registry" \
+    "${HOME}/.cargo/git"
+
+# Per-tool RUNs (caching).
+RUN --mount=type=secret,id=github_token,uid=1000,required=false \
+    --mount=type=cache,target=/home/agent/.cache/mise,uid=1000 \
+    GITHUB_TOKEN=$(cat /run/secrets/github_token 2>/dev/null || true) \
+    mise install "cargo-binstall@${CARGO_BINSTALL_VERSION}" && \
+    mise use -g --pin "cargo-binstall@${CARGO_BINSTALL_VERSION}"
+
+RUN --mount=type=secret,id=github_token,uid=1000,required=false \
+    --mount=type=cache,target=/home/agent/.cache/mise,uid=1000 \
+    --mount=type=cache,target=/home/agent/.cargo/registry,uid=1000 \
+    --mount=type=cache,target=/home/agent/.cargo/git,uid=1000 \
+    GITHUB_TOKEN=$(cat /run/secrets/github_token 2>/dev/null || true) \
+    mise trust /tmp/jackin-mise/mise.toml && \
+    mkdir -p "${HOME}/.config/mise" && \
+    cp /tmp/jackin-mise/mise.toml "${HOME}/.config/mise/config.toml" && \
+    : "Keep cargo-binstall pinned before installing Cargo-backed mise tools" && \
+    mise use -g --pin "cargo-binstall@${CARGO_BINSTALL_VERSION}" && \
+    mise install -C /tmp/jackin-mise rust && \
+    mise use -g --pin -C /tmp/jackin-mise rust && \
+    mise install && \
+    mise exec -- rustup component add rust-analyzer
+
+# cargo-binstall + caches.
+RUN --mount=type=secret,id=github_token,uid=1000,required=false \
+    --mount=type=cache,target=/home/agent/.cargo/registry,uid=1000 \
+    --mount=type=cache,target=/home/agent/.cargo/git,uid=1000 \
+    GITHUB_TOKEN=$(cat /run/secrets/github_token 2>/dev/null || true) \
+    . ~/.profile && \
+    cargo binstall --locked --no-confirm cargo-watch lychee
+
+RUN --mount=type=secret,id=github_token,uid=1000,required=false \
+    --mount=type=cache,target=/home/agent/.cache/mise,uid=1000 \
+    GITHUB_TOKEN=$(cat /run/secrets/github_token 2>/dev/null || true) \
+    mise install "opentofu@${OPENTOFU_VERSION}" && \
+    mise use -g --pin "opentofu@${OPENTOFU_VERSION}"
+
+RUN --mount=type=secret,id=github_token,uid=1000,required=false \
+    GITHUB_TOKEN=$(cat /run/secrets/github_token 2>/dev/null || true) \
+    mise exec -- npm install -g "ctx7@${CTX7_VERSION}" "skills@${SKILLS_VERSION}"
+
+# Caveman (opencode clone, codex/amp skills).
+RUN . ~/.profile && \
+    git clone --depth 1 --branch "v${CAVEMAN_VERSION}" https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman.git /tmp/caveman && \
+    node /tmp/caveman/bin/install.js --only opencode --no-mcp-shrink && \
+    test -f "${HOME}/.config/opencode/plugins/caveman/plugin.js" && \
+    skills add "JuliusBrussee/caveman#v${CAVEMAN_VERSION}" -a codex --yes --global && \
+    skills add "JuliusBrussee/caveman#v${CAVEMAN_VERSION}" -a amp --yes --global && \
+    test -f "${HOME}/.agents/skills/caveman/SKILL.md" && \
+    rm -rf /tmp/caveman
+
+# jackin-dev skills.
+RUN . ~/.profile && \
+    skills add "jackin-project/jackin-dev" -s '*' -a codex --yes --global && \
+    skills add "jackin-project/jackin-dev" -s '*' -a amp --yes --global && \
+    test -f "${HOME}/.agents/skills/jackin-propose/SKILL.md" && \
+    test -f "${HOME}/.agents/skills/jackin-merge-pr/SKILL.md"
+
+# improve skill (shadcn/improve).
+RUN . ~/.profile && \
+    skills add "shadcn/improve" -a claude-code --yes --global && \
+    skills add "shadcn/improve" -a codex --yes --global && \
+    skills add "shadcn/improve" -a amp --yes --global && \
+    skills add "shadcn/improve" -a opencode --yes --global && \
+    skills add "shadcn/improve" -a kimi-code-cli --yes --global && \
+    test -f "${HOME}/.claude/skills/improve/SKILL.md" && \
+    test -f "${HOME}/.agents/skills/improve/SKILL.md"
+
+# ── Token-optimisation stack ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+# AGENTS.md setup.
+RUN mkdir -p \
+    /home/agent/.config/caveman \
+    /home/agent/.claude \
+    /home/agent/.codex \
+    /home/agent/.config/amp \
+    /home/agent/.kimi-code \
+    /home/agent/.grok
+ENV CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE=ultra
+COPY --chown=root:agent --chmod=440 caveman-config.json /home/agent/.config/caveman/config.json
+COPY --chown=agent:agent --chmod=644 AGENTS.md.d/ /tmp/AGENTS.md.d/
+RUN find /tmp/AGENTS.md.d -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.md' | sort | \
+    while IFS= read -r file; do cat "${file}"; printf '\n'; done > /tmp/AGENTS.md && \
+    install -m 0644 /tmp/AGENTS.md /home/agent/AGENTS.md && \
+    install -m 0644 /tmp/AGENTS.md /home/agent/CLAUDE.md && \
+    ln -sf /home/agent/CLAUDE.md /home/agent/.claude/CLAUDE.md && \
+    ln -sf /home/agent/AGENTS.md /home/agent/.codex/AGENTS.md && \
+    ln -sf /home/agent/AGENTS.md /home/agent/.config/amp/AGENTS.md && \
+    ln -sf /home/agent/AGENTS.md /home/agent/.kimi-code/AGENTS.md && \
+    ln -sf /home/agent/AGENTS.md /home/agent/.grok/AGENTS.md
+
+# Headroom.
+RUN --mount=type=secret,id=github_token,uid=1000,required=false \
+    --mount=type=cache,target=/home/agent/.cache/mise,uid=1000 \
+    GITHUB_TOKEN=$(cat /run/secrets/github_token 2>/dev/null || true) \
+    mise install "uv@${UV_VERSION}" && \
+    mise use -g --pin "uv@${UV_VERSION}"
+
+RUN . ~/.profile && uv tool install --no-build "headroom-ai[mcp]==${HEADROOM_VERSION}"
+
+# PATH for shims.
+ENV PATH="/home/agent/.local/bin:/home/agent/.local/share/mise/shims:${PATH}"
+
+# RTK.
+RUN --mount=type=secret,id=github_token,uid=1000,required=false \
+    --mount=type=cache,target=/home/agent/.cache/mise,uid=1000 \
+    GITHUB_TOKEN=$(cat /run/secrets/github_token 2>/dev/null || true) \
+    mise install "rtk@${RTK_VERSION}" && \
+    mise use -g --pin "rtk@${RTK_VERSION}" && \
+    mise exec -- rtk --version
+
+ENV RTK_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
+
+# opencode RTK.
+RUN . ~/.profile && \
+    rtk init -g --opencode && \
+    test -f /home/agent/.config/opencode/plugins/rtk.ts

+# The Architect
+
+**The Architect** is the jackin agent role for developing [jackin](https://github.com/donbeave/jackin) itself (role identifier `the-architect`). It provides the Rust development environment needed to build and test the jackin CLI.
+
+`jackin` validates this repo's Dockerfile, derives the final image itself, and mounts the cached repo checkout into `/workspace` when you run:
+
+```sh
+jackin load the-architect
+# or, with the codex CLI instead of claude:
+jackin load the-architect --agent codex
+```
+
+In a Codex session, caveman is delivered through Codex skills under `~/.agents/skills` rather than the Claude plugin/statusline path; trigger it with text such as `caveman mode`. Claude-only UI pieces like the statusline badge and `/caveman` hook command are not expected there.
+
+## Contract
+
+- Final Dockerfile stage must use the digest-pinned `projectjackin/construct:<version>-trixie` base.
+- Plugins are declared in `jackin.role.toml`
+- Threat model and hard rules: see [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md)
+
+## Environment
+
+Jackin development tool versions come from [`jackin-project/jackin`](https://github.com/jackin-project/jackin). [`jackin-toolchain/mise.toml`](jackin-toolchain/mise.toml) is generated from the upstream `mise.toml` and keeps its tool pins plus the Cargo backend aliases/settings needed to install Rust tools through `cargo-binstall`. Comments and task definitions are intentionally omitted. [`jackin-toolchain/rust-toolchain.toml`](jackin-toolchain/rust-toolchain.toml) is copied from upstream as-is so Rust is installed from Jackin's tested toolchain file. Refresh both with `mise exec cargo:rust-script@0.36.0 -- scripts/update-jackin-toolchain.rs`; the scheduled `Jackin Toolchain` workflow opens a PR when upstream tool pins change.
+
+Architect-only bootstrap tools remain pinned in `Dockerfile` ARGs (`CARGO_BINSTALL_VERSION`, `OPENTOFU_VERSION`, `CAVEMAN_VERSION`, `CTX7_VERSION`, `HEADROOM_VERSION`, `UV_VERSION`, `RTK_VERSION`); bump via `docker build --build-arg <NAME>=<value>`.
+
+- **Jackin toolchain** (via mise): Node.js, Bun, Zig, Syft, Cosign, and Jackin's cargo tools from upstream `mise.toml` installed through `cargo-binstall`
+- **Rust** (via mise) with clippy, rustfmt, rust-analyzer
+- **Cargo helper tools**: cargo-watch and lychee
+- **Node.js** (via mise)
+- **Bun** (via mise) for jackin docs development
+- **OpenTofu** (via mise)
+- **Context7** (npm) — up-to-date library docs via MCP
+- **Caveman** token-compression hooks + skills (claude + codex profiles, pinned to a tagged release)
+- **Headroom** (uv tool) — MCP tools for compressing large context inputs
+- **RTK** (mise/aqua) — deterministic shell-output compression
+- System build tools (`build-essential`, `libssl-dev`, `pkg-config`, `cmake`)
+- **xxd** — hex dump and binary patch helper
+
+Shared shell/runtime tools come from `projectjackin/construct:trixie`.
+
+## Plugins
+
+Declared in [`jackin.role.toml`](./jackin.role.toml) under `[claude].plugins` and bootstrapped at runtime by jackin. Marketplaces beyond `@claude-plugins-official`:
+
+- `@jackin-marketplace` — [jackin-project/jackin-marketplace](https://github.com/jackin-project/jackin-marketplace) (source of `jackin-dev`)
+- `@tailrocks-rust-skills` — [tailrocks/tailrocks-rust-skills](https://github.com/tailrocks/tailrocks-rust-skills) (Rust guidance, project setup, review, refactoring, and remediation)
+- `@tailrocks-roadmap-skills` — [tailrocks/tailrocks-roadmap-skills](https://github.com/tailrocks/tailrocks-roadmap-skills) (research, brainstorming, planning, verification, and delivery)
+- `@caveman` — [JuliusBrussee/caveman](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman) (source of `caveman`; pinned to a tagged release via Dockerfile `CAVEMAN_VERSION`)
+
+Invoke these skills explicitly; the Roadmap pack covers proposal work through idea capture, research, and planning skills.
+
+Trust rationale: see [AGENTS.md § Threat model](./AGENTS.md#threat-model).
+
+## Skills
+
+Installed at build time via `skills add` for supported Agent Skills hosts (`claude-code`, `codex`, `amp`, `opencode`, and `kimi-code-cli`):
+
+- `improve` — [shadcn/improve](https://github.com/shadcn/improve): read-only advisor that audits a codebase and writes self-contained implementation plans under `plans/` for other agents to execute.
+
+## Runtime hooks
+
+The `hooks/preflight.sh` script runs before the agent CLI starts:
+
+1. **Context7** — non-interactive MCP setup (skips if unset).
+2. **Headroom MCP** — for active agent.
+3. **Caveman/RTK hooks** — for claude; skills for codex.
+4. **Codex caveman check**.
+
+## PR workflow
+
+Reference for which Claude Code review command to run at which point in a PR's life: see [`docs/pr-workflow.md`](./docs/pr-workflow.md).
+

+
+This project is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE).

+# Collateral gateway diagnosis
+
+**Scope:** read-only diagnosis of the original Homebrew OpenShell gateway and authentication path. No original gateway file, selected-gateway registry, service, or workload was changed or restarted. No workload was started. Temporary authenticated CLI profile was removed after the probe.
+
+## Workload state and event evidence
+
+`original-workload-states.json` records three pre-existing Docker containers as exited with code 137 and `OOMKilled=false`, with finish times clustered within 218 ms at 2026-10-23 22:14:39 UTC:
+
+- `openshell-default--coding-agents-00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`
+- `openshell-default--preview-openrouter-00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003`
+- `openshell-default--preview-docker-00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002`
+
+The captured Homebrew gateway log sequence is: each sandbox supervisor stream ended around 22:14:28; Docker reported supervisor-container exit status 137 around 22:14:29; the gateway changed phase from Provisioning to Error (`Sandbox failed to become ready`); then around 22:14:39 it logged `Stopped Docker sandbox after control supervisor failure`. This establishes the gateway's stop action happened after the supervisor failure. It does **not** establish who first terminated the supervisor containers or prove the initiating cause. The Docker state says not OOM-killed. Attribution of the initial signal remains unresolved.
+
+The earlier test-gateway configuration used the default `sandbox_label=default`, matching the installed gateway. The collateral time window overlaps the reported test activity, and a separate recorded namespace test later confirmed that two gateways sharing the default namespace can reconcile across one another. However, the retained :18770 startup log begins at 22:28:09Z, after these exits, and the initial gateway startup log was not retained. The exact test-gateway start time and causal link for these three exits remain unproven. Do not present namespace collision as established cause.
+
+## Original gateway and certificate findings
+
+- Original endpoint: `https://localhost:17670`, OpenShell 0.1.5, Docker driver.
+- Original service command uses `/opt/homebrew/var/openshell/gateway.toml`; that config has only `[openshell] version = 2` and `[openshell.gateway]`.
+- Installed service certificate material is under `/opt/homebrew/var/openshell/tls/`; the service launcher copies the CA and client cert/key into `~/.local/state/openshell/homebrew/tls/`.
+- The installed server certificate and installed client certificate both verify with `/opt/homebrew/var/openshell/tls/ca.crt` (`openssl verify`: `OK`). The installed client identity is `CN=openshell-client, OU=openshell-user`, SHA-256 fingerprint `7D:7C:8F:8A:47:B3:0D:22:33:2E:11:68:0E:67:71:DC:C5:0D:5A:BD:96:39:C7:BB:A3:55:6A:1C:A6:8D:03:1B`.
+- The registered user CLI profile at `~/.config/openshell/gateways/openshell/mtls/` contains a different CA and client certificate. Its client cert fingerprint is `B2:2F:00:73:DE:2E:00:3F:2C:46:A0:DB:CB:C3:47:10:7F:0A:D2:51:90:C9:2B:A4:93:AD:86:52:5C:F6:15:9B`; verification against the installed CA fails with `error 20 ... unable to get local issuer certificate`. The normal registered CLI request fails TLS peer verification with `BadSignature`. This is a certificate/profile mismatch before API authorization, not evidence of rejected sandbox permissions.
+
+## Authenticated owner API probe
+
+A temporary isolated `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` was populated with copies of the three installed client trust files (`ca.crt`, `client/tls.crt`, `client/tls.key`) under `openshell/gateways/openshell/mtls/`; key permissions were set to 0600. The command sequence was:
+
+```sh
+XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$probe/config" openshell gateway add --local --name openshell https://localhost:17670
+XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$probe/config" openshell --gateway openshell gateway info
+```
+
+Observed: registration succeeded, then `gateway info` returned `Status: healthy`, `Version: 0.1.5`, and Docker driver version `0.1.5`. Exit status 0. TLS verification remained enabled; no insecure flag was used. A read-only `sandbox list -o json` also succeeded with exit status 0. It returned these three names and IDs, each in phase `Error` and with condition reason `ControlSupervisorExited` / message `Docker supervisor container exited with status 137`: `preview-docker` (`00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002`), `preview-openrouter` (`00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003`), and `coding-agents` (`00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`). The temporary profile was removed. This gives the operator a safe authenticated API route: use an isolated temporary CLI profile populated from the installed gateway's own client CA/certificate/key. It does not alter the global CLI selection or stored credentials.
+
+## Temporary owner-profile recipe
+
+Only if an authorized operator needs the original gateway API, create a temporary directory and copy the installed owner identity into its local gateway profile. Never put the private key in evidence, logs, this repository, or a persistent CLI profile. Use mode 0600 for the key and remove the temporary directory when done:
+
+```sh
+profile=$(mktemp -d /tmp/ojp-owner.XXXXXX)
+mkdir -p "$profile/config/openshell/gateways/openshell/mtls"
+cp /opt/homebrew/var/openshell/tls/ca.crt "$profile/config/openshell/gateways/openshell/mtls/ca.crt"
+cp /opt/homebrew/var/openshell/tls/client/tls.crt "$profile/config/openshell/gateways/openshell/mtls/tls.crt"
+cp /opt/homebrew/var/openshell/tls/client/tls.key "$profile/config/openshell/gateways/openshell/mtls/tls.key"
+chmod 600 "$profile/config/openshell/gateways/openshell/mtls/tls.key"
+XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$profile/config" openshell gateway add --local --name openshell https://localhost:17670
+XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$profile/config" openshell --gateway openshell sandbox list -o json
+```
+
+The probe used only list/info operations. Restoration/start is a separate state-changing operation and was not run here.
+
+## Recovery boundary
+
+The authenticated owner API path is available for inspecting and operating known sandbox IDs. Any restoration should be a deliberate action by the primary operator, with IDs checked against `original-workload-states.json`; this diagnostic did not invoke start, restart, Docker start, or gateway restart. The original workloads' saved state was exited, so their previous process state cannot be reconstructed by this report.
+
+## v0.1.5 lifecycle source review and guarded plan
+
+The exact v0.1.5 server lifecycle source confirms the safe order for these retained `Error` records. `StopSandbox` accepts phase `Error` and intentionally invokes the normal compute-driver stop and supervisor-session cleanup; the source comment says an `Error` state does not prove compute has stopped. `StartSandbox` permits `Stopped`, `Completed`, `Starting`, or a failed main-process result (plus a timed-out provisioning recovery); a `ControlSupervisorExited` error is not a failed main-process result, so a direct start is rejected with a failed-precondition message directing the caller to stop first. Thus the API sequence is `stop` → wait `Stopped` → re-read and verify the same ID → `start` → wait `Ready`.
+
+Source references: [v0.1.5 compute lifecycle implementation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell/blob/v0.1.5/crates/openshell-server/src/compute/mod.rs#L1833-L1843) and [v0.1.5 start phase guard](https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell/blob/v0.1.5/crates/openshell-server/src/compute/mod.rs#L2033-L2065). The RPC handler authorizes `StartSandbox` against workspace and sandbox name before calling the compute lifecycle: [v0.1.5 gRPC handler](https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell/blob/v0.1.5/crates/openshell-server/src/grpc/sandbox.rs#L1799-L1834).
+
+SDK inspection used `uv run --with openshell==0.1.5`; no global SDK install was made. SDK `TlsConfig` accepts direct `Path` values for CA, client cert, and key; `SandboxClient` accepts the gRPC endpoint as `host:port` and TLS config. `SandboxClient.start`, `stop`, `get`, `wait_stopped`, and `wait_ready` are available. The SDK source is [v0.1.5 Python sandbox client](https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell/blob/v0.1.5/python/openshell/sandbox.py).
+
+A guarded, unexecuted plan is in [`experiments/collateral/restore-originals.py`](../../experiments/collateral/restore-originals.py). It uses the installed certificate paths directly, refuses to run without `--approved`, preflights all three exact IDs and `ControlSupervisorExited` states, rechecks identity/phase before each lifecycle change, uses only public OpenShell API stop/start operations, waits for `Stopped` and `Ready`, and writes state/action evidence without printing key bytes. No restore action has been run. The script passed an AST syntax parse and its SDK type/phase names were checked against the 0.1.5 package. Those checks do not prove restoration will succeed; readiness is only established if the authorized runtime execution succeeds.
+
+## Authorized restoration completed
+
+The user explicitly authorized corrective actions. The prepared guarded script was executed with `uv run --with openshell==0.1.5 python experiments/collateral/restore-originals.py --approved`. It used the existing installed gateway mTLS key paths directly, verified all target IDs/states before mutation, performed Stop then Start through the public SDK, and waited for Ready. No global registered certificate files were edited, private keys were not copied, and no TLS check was disabled. `restore-originals-execution.json` records all actions and PASS. `restoration-verification.json` records the same three sandbox IDs in Ready with harmless non-login-shell exec status 0 and expected stdout for each. The incident cause remains unproven; restoration does not retroactively establish the initiating actor.
+
+Restoration verifies current Ready/exec state and unchanged sandbox IDs. Original in-memory sessions and in-flight commands were not recovered or verified; no claim is made about their continuity.

+
+`cleanup.sh` sends SIGTERM to the experiment gateway PID whose command contains `experiments/gateway/gateway.toml`, then sleeps one second and removes `experiments/gateway/certs`, `state`, and `config`. +# Dedicated Docker engines: host-side fixture evidence
+
+Two disposable Docker-in-Docker engines ran outside OpenShell. They use image
+`docker:29.8.2-dind@sha256:1e08cdb63405ca788aea94ef35b792d1e299607c667d33d7bcbcae1fd2611ced`
+and Docker Engine `29.8.2` (commit `8af9fe3`). Outer engine: OrbStack Docker
+`29.8.2` on macOS 27.0 arm64. Each outer container has a 2 CPU and 4 GiB
+limit. No host Docker socket enters either container.
+
+Engine A uses `host.docker.internal:18776`, fixed service port `15432`, and
+auto-allocated service port `18080` from range `18080-18084`. Engine B uses
+`host.docker.internal:18777`, fixed service port `15433`, and auto-allocated
+service port `18088` from range `18085-18089`. The fixture sets each DinD
+container's `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` and publishes only its assigned
+small port range. Docker API is protected by mTLS. Each engine has a distinct
+CA and client certificate. No client private key is included in result files.
+
+OpenShell-approved named volumes `ojp-20261024-engine-a-project` and
+`ojp-20261024-engine-b-project` have labels
+`openshell.ai/sandbox-attachable=true` and
+`openshell.ai/sandbox-attachable-workspace=default`. The outer daemon mounts
+each at `/sandbox/ojp-project` inside its DinD container. The same absolute
+path is used for child-container bind mounts. Engine A and B use separate
+volumes. The Rust fixture was copied into both volumes. A child-container
+write was visible from the outer DinD container.
+
+## Results
+
+| Probe | Result | Mechanism | Evidence and boundary |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Valid mTLS API connection to A and B | PASS | EXTERNAL FIXTURE | `tls-probes.json`; host client only. |
+| Missing client certificate denied | PASS (expected denial) | EXTERNAL FIXTURE | TLS handshake says `tls: certificate required`. |
+| A client certificate rejected by B | PASS (expected denial) | EXTERNAL FIXTURE | B reports TLS certificate required; independent CA boundaries. |
+| Project-context image build on both engines | PASS | EXTERNAL FIXTURE | `api-probes.json`; actual Rust project supplied as context; small `Child.Dockerfile` copies it. Build times 1.78 s and 1.35 s. Nginx base image was pre-pulled; BuildKit did not report `CACHED` steps. This is not a Rust compile. |
+| Redis image for Compose/Testcontainers | PASS | WORKAROUND | `redis-image-seed.json`; `redis:7.4-alpine`, digest `sha256:57e4255cc971b1c8d8f6a8ca283ac01bc3ecdd914273ef6bfaede87aaecd6541` loaded into A, B, and Unix-socket engine by `docker save`/`docker load`. |
+| Container run, logs, exec, HTTP fixed port | PASS | EXTERNAL FIXTURE | `api-probes.json`; A `15432`, B `15433`. |
+| Docker automatic host port allocation | PASS | EXTERNAL FIXTURE | A `18080`, B `18088`; both within the forwarded ranges and HTTP-tested from host. |
+| Child bind mount and named volume operations | PASS | EXTERNAL FIXTURE | Child read `Cargo.toml` hash `ea3f8b22f608e82fb73f6f6c40e29dbec7f01bb03fef1517fb3ac8d011f617c6`; child write visible in source volume. Named volume create/write/inspect pass. |
+| Container removal | PASS | EXTERNAL FIXTURE | Temporary control containers removed after probes. |
+| Dedicated Unix socket API | PASS | EXTERNAL FIXTURE | `unix-socket-project.json`; Docker API listens on Unix socket only. Approved volume path `/sandbox/docker/docker.sock`; no Docker API port is published. Child-service port `18090` is the only outer TCP mapping. |
+| Unix socket access as UID 1000 | PASS after configuration | CONFIGURATION | Socket mode `0660` denied API access; `chmod 0666` allowed UID 1000. Any process with this volume mount receives full Docker-daemon authority. |
+| Shared project path on socket daemon | PASS | CONFIGURATION | `unix-socket-project.json`; approved project volume attached at `/sandbox/ojp-project` in DinD and intended same path in the OpenShell sandbox. Directory UID:GID `1000:1000`; UID 1000 wrote a file successfully. |
+| Interrupted provisioning cleanup | PASS | EXTERNAL FIXTURE | `interrupted-provision.json`; SIGKILL produced exit 137 and left container plus named and anonymous volumes. Fixture script removed only those resources and verified absence. |
+| Child-container local endpoint network | PASS | EXTERNAL FIXTURE | `child-network.json`; both nested engines' children reached experiment-owned Nginx endpoint on host port 15434 without OpenShell policy. This does not prove that Docker children inherit sandbox policy; it demonstrates an independent path requiring separate controls. |
+| Resource limits | PASS | EXTERNAL FIXTURE | `resource-limits.json`; outer DinD container caps aggregate daemon and children at 2 CPUs/4 GiB; child-specific 0.5 CPU/128 MiB limit appears in child cgroup. No OpenShell agent container was available for a live comparison. |
+
+The release also terminated an OpenShell sandbox when the project volume was
+mounted at `/workspace/ojp-project` (exit status 137). Parent evidence retains
+this failure. Moving both project mounts to `/sandbox/ojp-project` is a
+**Workaround**. It does not prove that the default workspace mount works.
+
+These results establish external daemon connectivity and API operation only.
+They do not establish that a Docker CLI or Testcontainers client inside an
+OpenShell sandbox can reach these engines, that OpenShell allows service
+connections on these ports, or that sandbox deletion removes daemon resources.
+The DinD containers, project volumes, images, and in-daemon resources belong
+to the experiment fixture. OpenShell has not removed them. The pre-Testcontainers
+inner-resource snapshot is in `inner-resource-ledger.json`: each TCP engine has
+its project-context image and named inner volume `ojp-20261024-engine-*-inner-volume`;
+Engine A also has the parent-owned `ojp-native-http` endpoint on port `15432`.
+Engine B and the Unix engine had no running inner containers at snapshot time.
+Inner images, containers,
+and volumes live in DinD's anonymous `/var/lib/docker` volume. The fixture
+cleanup script removes that data root with its owner DinD container, then
+removes only the explicitly named external project and socket volumes.
+
+An early Alpine HTTP control failed because that image lacked `httpd`; the
+failure is retained in `api-probes-initial-defect.json`. The corrected probes
+use pinned `nginx:1.29.3-alpine`.
+
+## Reproduction
+
+Run from `/Users/example/openshell-jackin-poc`:
+
+```sh
+experiments/engines/setup.sh
+experiments/engines/seed-image.sh
+python3 experiments/engines/seed-redis.py
+python3 experiments/engines/probe.py
+python3 experiments/engines/api-probes.py
+```
+
+`setup.sh` creates two privileged disposable DinD containers, which is needed
+for nested container execution. It fails if either named fixture container
+already exists. It creates experiment-only private keys under
+`experiments/engines/private`; those files stay out of the saved evidence.
+`seed-image.sh` transfers pinned Nginx image `nginx:1.29.3-alpine` from the
+host image store into each dedicated engine. It avoids the nested registry
+error `cannot assign requested address` observed during retest. This image
+transfer is a **Workaround** and does not prove registry access from a sandbox.
+`unix-socket.sh` creates an extra isolated DinD engine with an approved socket
+volume and project volume. It publishes child port `18090` only and narrows
+automatic host-port allocation to that single port for the database probe.
+The Docker API remains Unix-socket-only.
+`cleanup.sh` removes only the named experiment containers and project volumes,
+their anonymous DinD data volumes, and generated fixture keys. Run cleanup
+only after OpenShell sandbox experiments have ended and exported results.

+# macOS ARM64 VM profile result
+
+## Environment and versions
+
+The exact host release record is [`host-os.json`](host-os.json); the gateway TOML and captured startup log are preserved in [`gateway-config.toml`](gateway-config.toml) and [`gateway-startup.log`](gateway-startup.log). The libkrun process arguments confirming effective vCPU/memory values are in [`vm-launcher-before-delete.txt`](vm-launcher-before-delete.txt).
+
+- Host: macOS 27.0.1, build `26A434`, arm64 (Apple Silicon); raw `sw_vers` output is in [`host-os.json`](host-os.json). Docker endpoint is the existing OrbStack engine. No host Docker runtime was used for VM children.
+- OpenShell CLI, gateway, and VM driver: 0.1.5; source release commit `bdb956f2cd65a635f1294fccf1d138d263bf650f`.
+- VM backend: packaged `openshell-driver-vm` 0.1.5 with packaged libkrun/Hypervisor.framework path. The host already had a cached guest bootstrap rootfs and overlay template under the separate existing `preview-vm` profile; the new experiment used a dedicated runtime state/cache and prepared its own bootstrap and image disks.
+- Host image: `ojp-20261024-agent:2.1.310-poc-v3`, ID/digest `sha256:88b9118075feb284f28b34bb8baa4568aff8ab75c22022441e52a37079049ba4`, Linux arm64.
+- Guest sandbox name/ID: `ojp-20261024-vm1` / `c87a19b1-d941-4e22-a9cc-68d00be18b0f`. It ran under VM driver state `experiments/gateway-vm/state/runtime`, not Docker.
+- Gateway endpoint/name: `https://localhost:18771` / `ojp-20261024-vm`; mTLS and launch-scoped JWT enabled with credentials unique to this profile.
+- Resource request and effective configuration: create passed `--cpu 1 --memory 2Gi`, but the [v0.1.5 runtime documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/openshell/v0.1.5/how-it-works/sandboxes/runtimes) says MicroVM ignores those CLI CPU/memory requests. The gateway config set `vcpus = 2`, `mem_mib = 2048`, and `overlay_disk_mib = 4096`; the libkrun launcher process confirmed `--vm-vcpus 2 --vm-mem-mib 2048`. Thus actual configured allocation was 2 vCPUs, 2048 MiB guest memory, and 4 GiB writable overlay. Combined host+guest utilization was not sampled. This profile does not provide per-sandbox CPU/memory limits through the generic CLI; use VM gateway-wide config, which applies its fixed values to each sandbox.
+
+## Setup result
+
+`openshell-gateway config preflight --path experiments/gateway-vm/gateway.toml` initially failed with `inspect /usr/local/bin/mke2fs: Permission denied`. The user shell has a protected `/usr/local/bin`; the installed Homebrew e2fsprogs binaries are accessible at `/opt/homebrew/opt/e2fsprogs/sbin`. Prepending that directory made preflight pass and identified mke2fs, debugfs, and e2fsck as version 1.47.4. The profile's run script carries this PATH setting. No checks were disabled. See [`preflight-with-host-path.json`](preflight-with-host-path.json) and [`preflight-with-e2fsprogs.json`](preflight-with-e2fsprogs.json).
+
+The isolated gateway started, accepted mTLS, reported healthy, and advertised VM driver 0.1.5. The independent client alias was added in the profile XDG config, so global gateway selection remained unchanged. See [`info.json`](info.json), [`register.json`](register.json), and [`version.json`](version.json).
+
+## Runtime experiment
+
+The experiment used these commands:
+
+```sh
+experiments/gateway-vm/client.sh sandbox create \
+  --name ojp-20261024-vm1 \
+  --from ojp-20261024-agent:2.1.310-poc-v3 \
+  --policy experiments/denied.yaml \
+  --cpu 1 --memory 2Gi --no-auto-providers --detach \
+  -- bash --noprofile --norc -i
+
+experiments/gateway-vm/client.sh sandbox upload \
+  ojp-20261024-vm1 experiments/rust-project /sandbox/ojp-project
+
+experiments/gateway-vm/client.sh sandbox exec ojp-20261024-vm1 \
+  --workdir /sandbox/ojp-project/rust-project --no-login-shell -- claude --version
+```
+
+The `--upload` create flag cannot be combined with an explicit command in v0.1.5, so the project was transferred in a separate upload request. It is a copy: the guest source path has no live bind mount.
+
+The VM driver resolved both the bootstrap image `nvcr.io/nvidia/base/ubuntu:24.04` and the derived local agent image from the host's local container engine. It prepared a guest root disk, then reported the sandbox Ready with resolved workload UID:GID 1000:1000. Create began at 22:42:06.975 UTC; the first Ready observation was 22:43:18.974 UTC (~72 seconds cold). First successful compile completed at 22:44:08.894 UTC (~122 seconds from create). The prepared agent image ext4 file has 13 GiB logical size. This was a cold profile cache; local Docker image cache was warm, while the VM profile's bootstrap/prepared disk caches were cold. Gateway driver logs identify the local image digest and successful preparation; exact CLI results are [`create-vm1.json`](create-vm1.json), [`get-vm1-after-prep.json`](get-vm1-after-prep.json), and the later commands below.
+
+Claude's actual installed agent version ran successfully: `claude --version` returned `2.1.310 (Claude Code)`. Authenticated Claude operation was not tested; no provider credentials were attached. A `codex --version` probe failed because this image installs Claude Code, not Codex; see [`codex-version.json`](codex-version.json).
+
+The project had to be uploaded, then built using a per-command environment override:
+
+```sh
+experiments/gateway-vm/client.sh sandbox exec ojp-20261024-vm1 \
+  --workdir /sandbox/ojp-project/rust-project --no-login-shell -- \
+  env HOME=/home/agent \
+      MISE_DATA_DIR=/home/agent/.local/share/mise \
+      CARGO_HOME=/home/agent/.cargo \
+      RUSTUP_HOME=/usr/local/rustup \
+      MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS=/home/agent/ojp-toolchain:/workspace:/sandbox/ojp-project/rust-project \
+      PATH=/usr/local/cargo/bin:/usr/local/bin:/home/agent/.local/share/mise/shims:/home/agent/.local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin \
+      mise exec -- cargo build --locked --offline
+```
+
+The build exited 0 and compiled `runtime-probe`; output artifacts were under `/home/agent/.cache/mbx/targets/.../debug/libruntime_probe.rlib`. The build used the image's preinstalled Rust 1.99.1 and no network. Bare `cargo` and `mise exec -- cargo` failed first: the VM guest process environment exposed `HOME=/sandbox`, no `CARGO_HOME`, `RUSTUP_HOME`, or `MISE_DATA_DIR`, and a default PATH without Cargo. `mise exec` without explicit home/data settings attempted network downloads and failed under the default-deny policy. Supplying the known, non-secret image paths for one command restored the preinstalled toolchain. This profile therefore demonstrates agent/build capability with a **WORKAROUND**; the normal image environment is not automatically applied to the guest process in this run.
+
+Stop/start retained project files. The marker SHA-256 before and after was `3c181b2f9f8333addf46a991333a2e474fff87d8a32ae74943ce73160544e008`; both commands exited 0. See [`write-retained-file.json`](write-retained-file.json), [`stop-vm1.json`](stop-vm1.json), [`start-vm1.json`](start-vm1.json), and [`read-retained-file.json`](read-retained-file.json).
+
+## Interpretation
+
+**CONDITIONAL** for a Jackin integration prototype limited to a native VM agent plus explicit project upload and configured tool environment. The local ARM64 host, published v0.1.5 runtime, and packaged libkrun guest were sufficient to start a VM from the same v3 coding-agent image, run the agent's actual version, compile the Rust fixture, and retain files through stop/start. VM sandbox compute belongs to the VM driver, which owns the per-instance overlay. The driver retains prepared image disks as a separate profile cache until fixture cleanup. The project upload is a gateway-mediated copy, not a live mount. Generic `--cpu/--memory` requests are ignored by this driver; actual vCPU and memory values come from gateway-wide configuration.
+
+Docker API, Compose, Testcontainers, service ports, and VM-to-Docker child isolation were not tested in this profile. Do not infer Docker-child VM isolation from this successful VM agent test. Authenticated agent operation was not tested. Linux KVM, Docker Desktop, remote gateways, and Kubernetes remain untested here.
+
+The exact reproduction and each initial failure remain in this directory's individual JSON records. The disposable VM sandbox was deleted through OpenShell. The delete command exited 0; the next `get` returned “sandbox not found.” OpenShell removed its per-instance directory and 4 GiB overlay, and its VM helper and host supervisor processes exited. Its prepared image and bootstrap caches remained under the experiment state directory, totaling 6.2 GiB allocated (the prepared ext4 image's logical size was 13.6 GB). The scoped fixture cleanup then stopped only the `:18771` gateway and removed that experiment-owned cache, XDG client state, and ephemeral certificates. It preserved the gateway TOML and startup log as evidence. The existing `preview-vm` driver and VM processes remained live, with their runtime paths unchanged. See [`cleanup-inventory.json`](cleanup-inventory.json), [`sandbox-delete-vm1.json`](sandbox-delete-vm1.json), [`sandbox-get-after-delete.json`](sandbox-get-after-delete.json), [`profile-cleanup.json`](profile-cleanup.json), [`cleanup-inventory-after.json`](cleanup-inventory-after.json), [`vm-gateway-port-after-cleanup.json`](vm-gateway-port-after-cleanup.json), and [`preview-vm-still-active.json`](preview-vm-still-active.json). Before cleanup, the experiment state occupied 6.3 GiB; afterward the profile working directory was 40 KiB. The complete evidence directory occupies 132 KiB.

+# Isolated Docker gateway
+
+## Profile
+
+- Host: macOS 27.0 arm64, Apple T6050; 18 CPUs; 128 GiB RAM.
+- OpenShell release: `v0.1.5`, commit `bdb956f2cd65a635f1294fccf1d138d263bf650f`.
+- Gateway and CLI: `0.1.5`. Gateway binary SHA-256: `60b562d2d78cab122bd998f14f6b5a22f1a20e4bb77943a25498caee8d041ec9`.
+- Docker context: `orbstack`; endpoint `unix:///Users/example/.orbstack/run/docker.sock`; client `29.9.2`, engine `29.8.2`, Linux arm64.
+- Gateway name: `ojp-20261024-gw`; endpoint `https://127.0.0.1:18770`; bind address loopback only.
+- Gateway process is manually run outside OpenShell. PID at capture: `44804`. The dedicated state and CLI config directories are under this experiment directory.
+- mTLS CA, server and client credentials generated by the v0.1.5 `openshell-gateway generate-certs` command. Separate CA B used only for negative test. Private files mode `0600`; ignored by Git and excluded from evidence.
+- Docker driver: `0.1.5`; `allow_driver_config=true`; external resource admission stays enabled with default label requirements.
+
+## Reproduce
+
+1. Generate test credentials: `openshell-gateway generate-certs --output-dir /Users/example/openshell-jackin-poc/experiments/gateway/certs --server-san 127.0.0.1`.
+2. Run `experiments/gateway/run-gateway.sh` in a terminal. It listens on loopback port 18770. Keep that process running.
+3. In another terminal, run `OPENSHELL_LOCAL_TLS_DIR=/Users/example/openshell-jackin-poc/experiments/gateway/certs XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/Users/example/openshell-jackin-poc/experiments/gateway/config XDG_STATE_HOME=/Users/example/openshell-jackin-poc/experiments/gateway/state openshell gateway add https://127.0.0.1:18770 --local --name ojp-20261024-gw`.
+4. Run `experiments/gateway/client.sh status -o json`, `.../client.sh sandbox list -o json`, and `.../client.sh gateway info -o json`.
+
+This gateway uses TLS and mTLS client authentication. `--gateway-insecure` was used only for a negative test that isolates missing client authentication; the positive path verifies the server with the gateway CA. Never use the preliminary plaintext configuration for credentials or outside loopback.
+
+## Evidence
+
+See [evidence.md](evidence.md). No Jackin code or OpenShell source was changed. The gateway is not an OpenShell-managed companion. It remains an experiment-owned external gateway process; stop it with `Ctrl-C`. Do not delete the experiment directory before the parent `cleanup.sh` removes experiment-owned containers/resources.
+
+The Docker driver also requires the separate launch signer. `gateway.toml` explicitly points `[openshell.gateway.gateway_jwt]` at the generated `certs/jwt/` bundle. The gateway startup log must report `gateway-minted sandbox JWT enabled`. Listener mTLS alone can pass status/health checks while Docker sandbox creation fails with `docker sandboxes require launch-scoped gateway authentication`.

+# Gateway startup and mTLS evidence
+
+Release v0.1.5 (`bdb956f2cd65a635f1294fccf1d138d263bf650f`); host macOS 27.0 arm64; Docker endpoint OrbStack Unix socket. This is gateway setup evidence, not sandbox runtime proof.
+
+## Preliminary plaintext probe (retained)
+
+Command used isolated `XDG_STATE_HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` under `experiments/gateway`:
+
+```sh
+openshell-gateway --config experiments/gateway/gateway.toml --bind-address 127.0.0.1 --port 18770 --disable-tls --compute-driver docker
+OPENSHELL_GATEWAY_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:18770 openshell status -o json
+OPENSHELL_GATEWAY_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:18770 openshell sandbox list -o json
+```
+
+Result: **PASS** connectivity only. Gateway 0.1.5, Docker driver connected; empty sandbox list. Gateway logs warned `TLS disabled — listening on plaintext HTTP` and `the gateway has no authentication mechanism`. Process stopped before mTLS setup. Do not use this mode for any positive capability result.
+
+## mTLS gateway
+
+Config is in `experiments/gateway/gateway.toml`; launch command in `experiments/gateway/run-gateway.sh`. Release binary SHA-256 `60b562d2d78cab122bd998f14f6b5a22f1a20e4bb77943a25498caee8d041ec9`. Unique test PKI generated by:
+
+```sh
+openshell-gateway generate-certs --output-dir experiments/gateway/certs --server-san 127.0.0.1
+openssl verify -CAfile experiments/gateway/certs/ca.crt experiments/gateway/certs/server/tls.crt experiments/gateway/certs/client/tls.crt
+```
+
+Expected and observed: both generated certs verify against test CA; exit 0. Client certificate subject uses `OU=openshell-user`. No certificate/private-key bytes saved in evidence.
+
+First TLS startup failed, exit 1:
+
+```text
+configuration error: gateway TLS requires guest_tls_ca in [openshell.gateway] when using the docker compute driver
+```
+
+Added the generated CA as `guest_tls_ca`, required for Docker supervisor TLS. Same command then stayed live (PID `44804` at evidence capture). Logs: `TLS enabled — listening on encrypted HTTPS`; `TLS client certificate verification enabled`; `mTLS user authentication enabled`; `Compute driver connected configured_driver=docker advertised_driver=docker`; listener `127.0.0.1:18770`.
+
+Registration used the isolated XDG dirs and generated test PKI:
+
+```sh
+OPENSHELL_LOCAL_TLS_DIR=experiments/gateway/certs XDG_CONFIG_HOME=experiments/gateway/config XDG_STATE_HOME=experiments/gateway/state openshell gateway add https://127.0.0.1:18770 --local --name ojp-20261024-gw
+```
+
+Result: exit 0; `Gateway 'ojp-20261024-gw' added and set as active`; endpoint `https://127.0.0.1:18770`; `TLS certificates present`. Active selection and copied mTLS material live only under experiment XDG dirs.
+
+Positive checks:
+
+| Command | Result | Observed |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `experiments/gateway/client.sh status -o json` | PASS, exit 0 | `connected`, version `0.1.5`, authentication `authenticated`, provider `mTLS transport`. |
+| `experiments/gateway/client.sh sandbox list -o json` | PASS, exit 0 | Empty list. |
+| `experiments/gateway/client.sh gateway info -o json` | PASS, exit 0 | Gateway `healthy`; Docker driver `0.1.5`; no source extensions. |
+
+Negative auth checks:
+
+| Command | Result | Observed |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `openshell --gateway-endpoint https://127.0.0.1:18770 --gateway-insecure sandbox list -o json` without client cert | PASS (denial), exit 1 | `missing client certificate`; gateway records denied mTLS auth. Insecure server-verification bypass was only used to isolate the missing-client-cert check. |
+| `openssl s_client -brief -connect 127.0.0.1:18770 -CAfile certs/ca.crt -cert certs-b/client/tls.crt -key certs-b/client/tls.key </dev/null` | PASS (denial), exit 1 | TLS alert `decrypt error` after server cert verification; client B is signed by another generated CA. |
+
+## Result classification
+
+- Requirement: separate local gateway can run selected OpenShell release with Docker driver and mTLS.
+- Result: **PASS**.
+- Mechanism: **CONFIGURATION**.
+- Ownership: manually launched gateway process, experiment-owned SQLite state, isolated CLI registration, and generated test PKI. OpenShell sandbox lifecycle has not yet been tested here.
+- Limit: preliminary plaintext check does not prove secure auth. This setup is external to OpenShell lifecycle. Docker driver startup on OrbStack is proven; sandbox creation/stop/delete remain for parent experiments.
+- Docker resource admission remains enabled. `allow_driver_config=true` allows nonempty Docker driver config only. External Docker volumes still need approved labels `openshell.ai/sandbox-attachable="true"` and `openshell.ai/sandbox-attachable-workspace="default"`. No host bind mounts enabled.
+
+## Corrective setup after Docker launch denial
+
+Parent recorded a real sandbox-create failure in `results/basic/create.json`: OpenShell returned `docker sandboxes require launch-scoped gateway authentication` (exit 1). The existing listener used mTLS user authentication, but had no sandbox-launch signing keys. This error is retained unchanged.
+
+v0.1.5 documentation specifies a separate gateway JWT signing bundle. Added the release-supported `[openshell.gateway.gateway_jwt]` table to the isolated gateway config. It points to the existing experiment-owned files generated by `openshell-gateway generate-certs`: `jwt/signing.pem`, `jwt/public.pem`, and `jwt/kid`; gateway ID is `ojp-20261024`. `ttl_secs` omitted, matching documented local single-player Docker behavior. Listener mTLS remains enabled. Docker `allow_driver_config` and resource admission settings remain unchanged.
+
+Reproduction/validation:
+
+```sh
+openshell-gateway config preflight --path experiments/gateway/gateway.toml
+experiments/gateway/run-gateway.sh
+experiments/gateway/client.sh status -o json
+experiments/gateway/client.sh gateway info -o json
+curl --fail --cacert experiments/gateway/certs/ca.crt --cert experiments/gateway/certs/client/tls.crt --key experiments/gateway/certs/client/tls.key https://127.0.0.1:18770/.well-known/jwks.json
+```
+
+Preflight exit 0. Gateway startup log: `gateway-minted sandbox JWT enabled gateway_id=ojp-20261024`; TLS and mTLS remain enabled; Docker driver connects. mTLS CLI health reports `connected`, auth `authenticated`, version `0.1.5`. Gateway info reports `healthy`, Docker `0.1.5`. JWKS returns Ed25519 public signing key metadata; public key value omitted here. No sandbox was created by this corrective subtask. Parent must rerun the original creation command to prove launch works.
+
+- Requirement: Docker sandbox launch-scoped gateway auth is configured using released gateway config.
+- Result: **PASS** configuration and signer publication; sandbox create awaiting parent rerun.
+- Mechanism: **CONFIGURATION**.
+- Scope: no security check disabled; no Jackin or OpenShell source patch. Listener client authentication stays mTLS. Signing key material remains under ignored experiment `certs/` with private mode 0600.
+
+Source: [OpenShell v0.1.5 Gateway Configuration](https://docs.nvidia.com/openshell/v0.1.5/how-it-works/gateways/configuration), section `gateway_jwt`; listener TLS and sandbox launch signing use separate keys, and v0.1.5 local config uses `signing_key_path`, `public_key_path`, `kid_path`, and `gateway_id`.
